scope: Windows PCs and Android phones; opt-in relays; 800 m route target, 1 km stretch, radius coverage separate
coverageMeaning: lab-covered means an identified synthetic test exercises a limited protocol property. It does not pass hardware or production gates. This register is extensible, not exhaustive.

scenarios.scenario: Fresh installation defaults relay mode off and refuses unauthorized circuits
Relay enable/disable, stop and revocation take effect on existing and pending circuits
Three Windows PCs sustain simultaneous inbound and outbound RFCOMM on real adapters
Relay discovery rejects headsets, unpaired devices, spoofed names and unrelated services
Separate relay service UUID cannot bypass the existing document service authentication
Per-neighbor admission, byte limits, deadlines and global concurrency enforce bounded CPU and memory
Slowloris, idle handshakes and connection floods do not starve local editing
Real relay logs, diagnostics, crash dumps and error paths contain no document titles, invitation secrets, keys or content
Malformed route-setup fields, huge lengths, unknown versions and illegal states fail closed
Race detector, parser fuzzing, resource soak and goroutine/leak checks pass with supported toolchains
Physical relay reboot, radio toggle, adapter removal and Windows sleep/wake do not lose committed endpoint edits
Existing direct-sharing app and old packages do not mistake experimental circuits for normal connections
Native Android APK builds reproducibly, is signed for testing and installs without cloud dependencies
Denied, revoked and one-time Nearby devices permissions produce clear recoverable states
Foreground relay opt-in, ongoing notification, explicit stop and service lifecycle comply with target OS versions
Screen off, Doze, battery saver, low battery and OEM process management are tested on named hardware
Force-stop, process death, reboot and app removal end relay service without claiming it is available
Windows–Android–Windows forwarding passes endpoint identity and exact payload tests on physical devices
Android–Windows–Android forwarding passes endpoint identity and exact payload tests on physical devices
Android endpoint TLS trust manager validates the exact intended certificate without trusting every self-signed certificate
Both endpoint roles and relay roles interoperate across supported OS/TLS provider versions
Android backup, logcat, notification text, WebView bridge and debug builds do not expose invitations or payloads
Discovery authenticates peers and uses expiring opaque routing handles without document metadata
Loops, duplicate discovery, stale routes and hop-limit exhaustion terminate within bounded work
Maliciously small or forged hop counts cannot create unbounded forwarding
Two or more simultaneous routes and competing documents remain isolated
No available next hop, missing relay software or an unpowered relay reports no route
Relay churn, movement, route flapping and reconnection use bounded backoff and avoid flood amplification
Sybil peers, route poisoning, blackholes and colluding relays have assessed limits and do not bypass endpoint identity
Destination authentication fails when a relay redirects a circuit to another endpoint
Multiple peers behind a relay, fairness and backpressure do not grow unbounded queues
Cross-circuit, cross-direction and cross-session replay attempts are rejected end to end
Path replacement starts fresh authentication and merges missing edits from destination/source journals
Only the actual destination journal commit produces a document acknowledgement
Relay acknowledgement, link-connect state and intermediary byte receipt never count as saved/synchronized
Endpoint crash at every journal/checkpoint/ack boundary preserves committed edits and recovers unacknowledged updates
Disk full, quota failure, stale tabs and corrupt journals remain visibly recoverable through a relayed connection
Simultaneous formatted edits, large updates, undo, history and Unicode converge after route failure and both endpoint restarts
Invitation distribution, revocation, expiry, clock skew and rotation have explicit threat-reviewed behavior
TLS downgrade, algorithm negotiation, resumed sessions and any future early-data behavior have an interoperability/replay review
Timing/size/adjacency leakage is documented; any padding design is measured and does not claim anonymity
No route or failure silently falls back to Wi-Fi, Internet, cloud, analytics or external DNS
Runtime flags, separate package, document compatibility, rollback and upgrade paths preserve the user-confirmed stable release
Measure every adjacent link and sustained end-to-end delivery over an 800 m route with documented node positions
Measure an optional 1 km route separately without treating it as achieved by the 800 m result
If an 800 m radius is required, verify multiple bearings and coverage gaps separately from a single straight route
Walls, concrete, floors, vegetation, rain, crowds and 2.4 GHz interference are recorded as tested conditions
Moving endpoints, moving relays, changing body orientation and hidden terminal effects are characterized
Measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, reconnect time and loss against hop count
Typing/save latency remains acceptable while relaying under CPU, memory and radio contention
Overnight and multi-day relay soak records battery drain, thermals, storage, memory and disconnects
Small updates, near-limit documents and competing traffic pass supported-load limits
Independent threat-model, cryptographic integration and adversarial implementation review resolves critical/high findings
Release-specific dependencies, native/Android toolchains and TLS providers pass vulnerability and license review
Reproducible signed installer/APK, clean offline install, crash reporting privacy, backup and rollback are exercised
Publish a supported Windows/Android hardware matrix, measured limitations and repeatable field/security evidence
